report_raw.claim: Why should you pay more taxes than Donald Trump pays? And that’s a fact. $750. Remember what he said when that was raised a while ago, how he only pays … He said, ‘Because I’m smart. I know how to game the system.’
report_raw.justification: The New York Times reported, based on Trump’s tax-return data, that his federal income tax was $750 in each of 2016 and 2017; the figure does not represent all types of taxes. [S1][S3] Tax Policy Center models estimated that about half of U.S. tax units paid more than $750 in federal income tax in each of those years, but that does not establish what any particular listener paid. [S5] The attributed remark misstates the relevant exchange: in a 2016 debate, Trump said “That makes me smart” after Hillary Clinton referred to earlier years in which he had paid no federal income tax. [S7] The $750 figures were reported in 2020, so that debate remark was not a response to those figures. [S7][S9] The supplied evidence does not establish that Trump said the additional attributed words, “I know how to game the system,” on another occasion.
key_points: The $750 figure refers to reported federal income tax in 2016 and 2017, not all taxes. [S1][S3]
An estimated half of U.S. tax units paid more than $750 in federal income tax in each year; individual listeners’ payments are unknown. [S5]
Trump’s documented 2016 remark was “That makes me smart,” in response to a claim about earlier years, not the later-reported $750 figures. [S7][S9]
The evidence does not rule out Trump using the phrase “I know how to game the system” on another occasion.
report_raw.counter_argument: A case for a more favorable verdict is that the $750 figure is supported by detailed reporting, about half of tax units paid more, and Trump did say “That makes me smart” about paying no federal income tax. [S1][S5][S7] The claimed quotation could be read as a loose paraphrase of that exchange. But the statement presents different words as a direct quotation and links the remark to the $750 figure, which was reported years later. [S7][S9]
evidence_gaps: The underlying tax-return data were not publicly released at the time; the other cited reporting relies on the Times investigation rather than independently examining the records.
Evidence of whether Trump used the exact phrase “I know how to game the system” on another occasion would clarify that part of the attribution.
No particular listener’s federal income tax payment is specified, so the individual comparison cannot be verified.

findings.question: For the tax year or years associated with the $750 figure, how did that amount compare with federal income taxes paid by other U.S. taxpayers?
findings.summary: The New York Times reported that Trump paid $750 in federal income taxes in each of 2016 and 2017. According to Tax Policy Center models, about half of U.S. tax units paid more than $750 in federal income tax in each of those years. Separately, the Congressional Budget Office estimated that households in the middle 20% of the income distribution paid an average of $2,200 in federal income taxes in 2016. These comparisons do not establish what any particular listener paid.

sources.title: Donald Trump paid $750 in income tax in 2017. About half of Americans paid more.
sources.snippet: Mark Mazur, the director of the Tax Policy Center (America’s leading nonpartisan tax think tank) and a former assistant secretary for tax policy at the Treasury Department, told me that according to TPC’s models, about half of American tax units* paid more than $750 in federal income taxes in 2016 and 2017.

sources.title: Trump likely paid less in federal income tax than average middle-class American
sources.snippet: In 2016, households in the middle 20 per cent of the US income distribution paid an average of $2,200 (£1,711) in federal income taxes, according to the Congressional Budget Office, a nonpartisan government agency.

caveats: A tax unit can include nonfilers and is not necessarily the same as a household or an individual taxpayer.
The $2,200 figure is a group average, not the amount paid by every middle-income household. The comparisons concern federal individual income tax, not all taxes.

findings.question: Did Donald Trump say 'Because I’m smart' and 'I know how to game the system' in response to the $750 tax figure or another question about his taxes, and what was the context?
findings.summary: At the September 26, 2016 debate, Trump said, “That makes me smart,” after Hillary Clinton referred to records showing he had paid no federal income tax in certain earlier years. He was not responding to the $750 figure: that figure for 2016 and 2017 was reported in September 2020. The debate transcript does not include the attributed words “I know how to game the system”; in a later 2016 debate, Trump did say he understood the tax code better than anyone who had run for president.

TRUMP: That makes me smart.
